To summarize, the key findings of our research, stated in one sentence that includes all relevant information, are that

(1) the problem of embedding a graph G into a topological surface can be efficiently solved on-line, (2) the complexity of the problem is closely related to the genus of the topological surface, and (3) the problem is efficiently solved in the range of genus k, 1 ≤ k ≤ O(n^(1/2)) for general graphs, and in the range of 1 ≤ k = O(n^(1-1/m)) for planar graphs with m faces.

(i) the new data structure for embeddings of graphs is superior to the previously used data structures; (ii) the problem of constructing an embedding of a graph into a surface of fixed genus is polynomial time solvable for a large class (including the class of planar graphs) of graphs and for a large range (including the range 0 to 4) of the genus; (iii) the problem of embedding a graph with a fixed number of edges and a fixed number of crossings into
the problem “given G, construct a genus-k embedding for G” can be solved for k = 2 in O(n log n) time, k = 3 in O(n2) time, k >= 4 in O(n3) time and k >= 6 in O(n4) time.
In summary, our research is concerned with
the problem of representing a graph by means of a drawing in which each vertex is represented by a point and each edge is represented by a curve that connects the corresponding pair of points.
the following three questions: (a) What is the complexity of graph embedding?

the following questions: (1) What is the computational complexity of the problem “given an embedding for a graph, construct a graph that realizes this embedding”? (2) How can we efficiently represent a given embedding?
In summary, a comprehensive and detailed conclusive statement would be that
for a large class graphs and for a large range, the problem “given an integer k, find a genus k embedding of the graph” can be efficiently solved.
the problem of embedding a graph in a topological surface is a very difficult problem, but that there are a number of special cases where the problem can be solved efficiently.
the problem of constructing a genus g embedding of a graph G can be solved in time linear in the number of vertices of the graph G, for every fixed g.
A comprehensive summary for our work would be that
we have developed a general framework for the study of the computational complexity of graph embedding problems.
we have solved a number of long-standing open problems in the field of graph embedding.
for a large class (including planar, series-parallel, outerplanar, and k-trees) of graphs, we have developed efficient algorithms to construct a graph embedding into a surface of any genus.
The main takeaway from our work is that
the problem of graph embeddings can be solved efficiently in a variety of cases, even when the graph is dense and the genus is large.
the complexity of embedding a planar graph into a surface of genus k is Θ(n log k) where n is the size of the graph.
the complexity of embedding a planar graph is not the same as the complexity of embedding an arbitrarily high genus graph.
